name: Glacier
desc: A valley glacier system seen from above — ice piles up above the snowline and streams down its troughs, rock spalled off the valley walls rides on its back, and where two tributaries merge their debris stripes weld into a medial moraine that runs the length of the tongue; the snowline wanders over minutes so the terminus advances and retreats, stranding a new moraine arc at every stand while the ice grinds its trough deeper.

energy.doc: mass-balance and abrasion vigour — how hard the ice grows and carves — plus colour/contrast gain

scale.doc: magnification into the icefield around x/y — 1 shows the whole system, 2.6 crops to the snout

speed.doc: rate of flow, carving and the advance/retreat cycle

density.doc: wall-debris supply — how heavily the ice is striped with moraine

climate.doc: climate: 0 = a warm shrunken tongue barely holding its cirque, 1 = a glacial maximum filling every trough to the outlet

hue.doc: ice hue anchor; rotates the plate with it

x.doc: view centre x (only bites when scale > 1)

y.doc: view centre y (only bites when scale > 1)

style.doc: aesthetic: aerial = blue-white ice with dark debris stripes welding into medial moraines over ochre moraine arcs; hypsometric = false-colour elevation ramp + hillshade; radar = abstracted, the ice mass as a bright plate on near-dark ground; ink = sumi tonal wash
